title: No random-example cost
statement: For a small-bias Fourier estimation input whose accuracy data satisfy $n>0$, positive numerator, and twice the numerator at most the denominator, and whose Fourier bound is at least $1$, the estimator's random-example cost is zero for every finite coordinate set $U$ in the input dimension.
hypotheses_covered: Twice the accuracy numerator is at most its denominator
$U$ is a finite set of coordinates in the input dimension
